body.cap: The M.E.N.D. BioSimulator showcased the ‘CARDIOS’ solution for automatic cardiovascular disease risk prediction at CES 2024. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The M.E.N.D. BioSimulator, led by CEO Lee Jun-sang, participated in CES 2024 held in Las Vegas from January 9th to 12th.

The M.E.N.D. BioSimulator provides an automatic cardiovascular disease risk prediction solution using precision 3D vascular models and artificial intelligence-based algorithms. The company’s flagship software, CARDIOS (Coronary Artery Risk Diagnostics Integrating On-site Software), automatically acquires a 3D cardiovascular model from patients’ X-ray and CT images. It performs high-dimensional operations to identify the major lesions in the cardiovascular system within minutes.

According to officials, this solution enables non-invasive, AI-based, and accurate data-driven cardiovascular diagnostic factor predictions throughout the entire process from pre-diagnosis to treatment. Skipping the probing process required for patient visits and tests for cardiovascular diagnostic factor measurements can lead to significant cost savings in the treatment process.

CARDIOS automates the entire process required for cardiovascular diagnosis, allowing immediate use in medical settings without the assistance of external experts. Moreover, by utilizing vascular shape data, blood flow data, and patient physiological data directly from the medical field, the system prevents the leakage of medical clinical data to external sources.

An official from The M.E.N.D. BioSimulator stated, “This solution enhances the possibility of early diagnosis through the utilization of health checkups and can also be used for procedure prognosis monitoring. It has achieved 98% accuracy compared to conventional testing methods and can produce diagnostic results within 5 minutes.”

body.cap: Demo video of The M.E.N.D. BioSimulator’s Solution | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The M.E.N.D. BioSimulator introduced a range of AI-based medical software and physiological monitoring systems at CES 2024, including MIASfacial (Facial Asymmetry Quantification and Filler Procedure Monitoring System), N-UDS (Non-invasive Urodynamic Test System), Blood Glucose Monitoring System (System predicting and monitoring blood glucose levels using real-time biosignal data measured through wearable devices), and CBCT Denoising sCT System (CBCT Image Noise Reduction System). Through these innovations, the company aims to secure independent influence in the global medical device market.

The official further emphasized, “While focusing on securing certification and inspection institution infrastructure using our software and devices domestically, our goal is to enhance momentum for market expansion and global business development in the future. We aim to become a global company by attracting organic cooperation with local insurers and medical device distributors in North America, etc.”

They continued, “During the exhibition period, we introduce the company through consultations with various companies from different countries. Additionally, we anticipate creating valuable opportunities by meeting with participating startup companies.

We want to engage in more discussions with companies wishing to collaborate or receive our technology, especially those in the United States and Japan. We plan to achieve over KRW 30 billion in sales by 2027, securing a main business. Starting with inspection institutions, between 2024 and 2027, we intend to expand our revenue model through annual subscriptions, indefinite licenses, and additional CT services, intensifying our focus on the health checkup market following the aging trend.”

body.x: CES, the world’s largest IT exhibition organized by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), is held in Las Vegas every January, providing a comprehensive view of global technology industry trends. AVING News, covering CES for 18 consecutive years, has been selecting the best innovative products, companies, and technologies and conducting ‘BEST OF CES’ and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA’ selections. Additionally, through ‘AVING LIVE,’ they provide live coverage of CES issues.

The CES 2024 Seoul Pavilion operated on the most historical scale since Seoul’s first participation in CES in 2020, with the largest exhibition area, number of participating companies, and supporter numbers. Seoul Metropolitan Government collaborated with 13 institutions to design The Seoul Pavilion, which is essential in Seoul’s endeavors to establish Seoul as a startup hub. Among the participating companies in the Seoul Pavilion, 17 received innovation awards, proving their capabilities. Collaborated institutions include Seoul Business Agency, Seoul Bio Hub, Seoul Campus Town, Yangjae Innovation Hub, Gwanak-gu, Yonsei University, Korea University, Chung-Ang University, Sogang University, Kookmin University, Hanyang University, and Kyunghee University, totaling 13. Seoul City and institutions and supporters participating in industry-academic cooperation are matched 1:1 with companies, with a maximum of 85 supporters participating.
